notes.meaning: As the Sabbath ended and the first day of the week began to dawn, Mary Magdalene and another Mary went to visit the tomb of Jesus. They had rested on the Sabbath day in deep sorrow and were now returning to where He was buried. The fact that women were the first to visit and witness the tomb shows the honesty of the story, since ancient society often looked down on the testimony of women.

A powerful shaking took place when an angel sent from God came down from heaven. The angel rolled the heavy stone away from the entrance and sat on it in victory. Jesus did not need the stone moved in order to get out, but it was moved so people could see that the tomb was empty.

The angel shone with brilliant light like flashes of lightning, showing his heavenly glory. His clothing was pure white like snow. This pure white appearance was a sign of his holy innocence and the good news he brought.

The Roman soldiers stationed to guard the tomb were terrified by the angel. Even though they were tough, battle-tested men, they shook with fear and fainted like dead men. God showed that human strength and weapons could not keep Jesus in the grave.

The angel spoke kindly to the women and told them not to be afraid. While the Roman guards had reason to shake in fear, those who seek Jesus have no reason to be terrified. The angel honored their faithful love for the Lord who had died on the cross.

The angel announced that Jesus was no longer in the grave because He had risen, exactly as He had promised before His death. The angel invited the women inside to see the empty shelf where His body had been placed. Seeing the empty tomb gave them clear proof that His body was truly gone.

The angel gave the women an urgent job to tell the disciples that Jesus was alive from the dead. Jesus was already on His way ahead of them to Galilee, where they would all see Him together. God gave these devoted women the special honor of being the very first to announce the good news to the apostles.

The women quickly ran from the tomb, feeling both awe and wonderful excitement. They rushed to carry the message to the grieving disciples. Great news about the risen Lord naturally fills the heart with both holy fear and deep joy.

While the women were on their way, Jesus Himself suddenly met them and greeted them warmly. They fell before Him, clasped His feet in love, and worshiped Him as their living Lord. Holding His feet showed that He was not a ghost, but had truly risen in a real body.

Jesus comforted the women, telling them not to be afraid, and repeated the call to meet Him in Galilee. By calling the disciples His brothers, He showed that He fully forgave them for abandoning Him when He was arrested. He welcomed them back with family warmth rather than scolding them.

While the women ran to tell the disciples, some of the guards went into Jerusalem to report everything to the chief priests. The soldiers gave an honest account of the earthquake and the angel because they had to explain why the tomb was open and the body was missing. They turned to the Jewish leaders who had posted them at the grave.

The chief priests called an urgent meeting with the Jewish elders to figure out what to do. Rather than admitting the truth of the resurrection, they decided to pay the soldiers a large sum of money. They used bribery to try to cover up the miracle.

The leaders commanded the soldiers to spread a lie that the disciples had stolen the body while the guards slept. This story was full of holes, because sleeping guards could never know who had come or what had happened. Even so, the enemies of Jesus were desperate for an excuse to deny the truth.

Falling asleep on guard duty was a serious crime that could cost a Roman soldier his life. The Jewish leaders promised that if Governor Pilate found out, they would talk to him and keep the guards out of trouble. They were confident they could use their influence to protect the soldiers.

The soldiers took the bribe and told the lie they were taught to say. Matthew notes that this story was still widely spread among the Jewish people many years later when he wrote his book. People who harden their hearts against the truth will often believe a clumsy lie instead.

The eleven disciples obeyed Jesus and traveled north to Galilee. They went up the specific mountain where Jesus had directed them to meet Him. There were only eleven of them now, because Judas was gone.

When the disciples saw Jesus, they fell to the ground and worshiped Him as the divine Son of God. Some of them struggled with doubt at first, feeling stunned by the sight or seeing Him from a distance before He came close. Their initial doubt shows they were honest men who only believed after seeing solid proof.

Jesus walked up to them and announced that God the Father had given Him all authority in heaven and on earth. As the risen Savior, He holds total power over the entire universe. His followers can step out in faith knowing that their Lord has supreme rule over all things.

Because Jesus holds all power, He commanded His followers to go and make disciples among all the nations of the world. A disciple is someone who turns from sin, trusts in Jesus, and follows His teachings. He directed them to baptize these new followers into the shared name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

differ.view: Making disciples of nations includes baptizing the children of believers before they are taught, just as Jewish infants were circumcised into the covenant before receiving instruction.
Making disciples requires hearing and personal faith before baptism, so baptism should be given only to those who have been taught and believe.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars doubt that Jesus spoke these words about Father, Son, and Spirit, thinking them too developed for his time. Others defend them as genuine.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: The Orthodox Church baptizes by dipping a person three times, once for each name.

notes.meaning: Jesus instructed the disciples to teach new believers to obey everything He had commanded them. He closed with a wonderful promise: He would be with them continually through His Spirit until the very end of time. His constant presence gives believers the power and courage to live for Him every day.
